I'm just glad to hear that we punish people down here for breaking the rules. Is that just for Vault dwellers or for people who come down here and murder Vault dwellers?|Norm to [[Betty Pearson]]|sound=Norm MacLean.ogg}} '''Norman "Norm" MacLean''' is a resident of [[Vault 33]] in [[Timeline#2296|2296]]. He is the inquisitive brother{{Ref|(Age)}} of [[Lucy MacLean]] and the son of [[Hank MacLean]]. He takes on a role as a deuteragonist in the story of the TV series once he begins exploring the mystery behind [[Vault 32|Vaults 32]] and [[Vault 31|31]]. ==Background== Norm was born to [[Rose MacLean|Rose]] and [[Hank MacLean]] of Vault 33 and has one sister, [[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]].[[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 1 character description on Amazon]]: ''"The younger brother of Lucy, and a bit of a black sheep in the Vault 33 community. Despite not fitting in and lacking enthusiasm in every job he’s ever been assigned, he is deeply loyal to his community. Vault 33 is his home."'' Rose suspected the surface world was hospitable and fled Vault 33, angering her husband because he viewed this as dangerous. Rose took Norm and his older sister to live in [[Shady Sands]], although the two children seemed too young to have memories of being on the surface. At some point, Hank finds Rose on the surface, but she refuses to return with him. Hank took his children back from Rose, moving them back to Vault 33, where they believed Rose had died of natural causes during their early childhood.{{FOTV|1|8}} [[File:Hank Lucy and Norm.png|thumb|250px|Norm with his father and sister]] Growing up in Vault 33, Norm became best friends with his cousin [[Chet (TV series)|Chet]]. However, he is a black sheep in the Vault's community due to his introversion and irreverent personality. As he came to working age, Norm went from job to job in the Vault, receiving a performance grade of "lacks enthusiasm" at each one. Despite his general apathy, he does care about the community to some degree, especially the people who are close to him.[https://web.archive.org/web/20240114045401/https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/11/fallout-first-look Vanity Fair: "Fallout First Look: This Is How the World Ends—With a Smiling Thumbs-Up" (Archived)] ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== {{Quotation|The younger brother of Lucy, and a bit of a black sheep in the Vault 33 community. Despite not fitting in, and lacking enthusiasm in every job he’s ever been assigned, he is deeply loyal to his community. Vault 33 is his home.|[[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 1 character description]]}} ====[[The End (episode)|The End]]==== Norm discovers the residents of [[Vault 32]] are all dead just before an attack by [[Vault 32 raider|raiders]] posing as [[Vault 32 dweller|residents]]. During the attack, he hides in a storage space under the floor. [[File:FOTV Official Trailer Still 054.png|thumb|250px|left|Norm hugging Lucy goodbye]] After the attack, Norm's sister Lucy proposes they send a search party to the surface to find their kidnapped dad. However, the interim council rejects her proposal based on keeping the Vault safe, although Norm speculates they did so because they don't want to recover their father, and since then, they wouldn't be in charge anymore. He later helps his sister Lucy leave the vault and they share a brief hug.{{FOTV|1|1}} ====[[The Head]]==== [[File:FOTV The Head Norm.png|thumb|250px|Norm waiting for his punishment]] Due to helping his sister escape, the Vault council comprised of [[Woody Thomas]], [[Reg McPhee]], and [[Betty Pearson]] decide to punish Norm with a demotion. The council scolds Norm, saying he and Chet put their Vault in incredible danger since the radiation levels could have killed everyone and the last vestiges of human civilization. Norm attempts to defend himself saying it was Lucy's idea. When the council points out he could have tried to stop her, Norm replies it was not on his mind. He is reassigned from computer duty to delivering food to the surviving raiders, even after he suggests the raiders deserve punishment. He later suggested executing the imprisoned raiders in the Vault during an assembly, causing many of the dwellers to be disgusted at him and his idea. Betty rejects the idea, saying murdering them should be out of the question. Norm then, perhaps snarkily, apologizes to Betty for questioning her leadership. After the meeting, [[Steph Harper]] approaches Norm to tell him she agrees with his idea of executing the raiders.{{FOTV|1|3}} ====[[The Ghouls]]==== [[File:Betty brings pie.png|thumb|left|250px|Betty imploring Norm to tread lightly]] Betty brings some pie she made herself to Norm. She comes to talk to him about how his vocalizing his desire to kill the raiders upset the Vault dwellers and that what he says carries weight because he is the only MacLean left in the Vault. Norm expresses how he feels guilty about hiding during the raid, and Betty notices how he feels angry about it. Betty comments that because Norm is clever, how he channels his anger can lead to dark places, and asks him to tread lightly before she leaves. While delivering food to the raiders, Norm has a small talk with [[Veronica (TV series)|Veronica]] about how she feels the raiders do not deserve cake. Veronica wants some of the cake herself, so Norm secretly gives her the cake instead of the raiders. Once Veronica has left, Norm talks to one raider, [[Dervin]], who claims that the raiders did not kill the dwellers of Vault 32, and that the dwellers were not as innocent as Norm thinks. Afterward, Norm tries to look into files related to Vault 32, but his access is denied. He goes to Chet for help getting into Vault 32, whose door had been damaged in an explosion and was accessible if they moved some rubble. The pair explore Vault 32 and find that the dwellers had all died at least two years ago in what appeared to be internal conflict, meaning the raiders did not kill the residents. They eventually reach the overseer's office, finding the [[Ian Jackson|deceased overseer]]'s corpse; Norm accesses the overseer's terminal and finds that his mother [[Rose MacLean|Rose]]'s Pip-Boy was used to access Vault 32 from the surface.{{FOTV|1|4}} ====[[The Past]]==== [[File:The Past Vault 32 paint job.png|250px|thumb|Norm looking at the freshly painted Vault 32]] Exploring Vault 32, still confused as to how the Vault 32 raiders had his mother's Pip-Boy, Norm and Chet discover that many of the Vault 32 dwellers died trying to get into [[Vault 31]]. They hurriedly return to Vault 33 to try to avoid suspicion, but are seen not far away from the Vault 31 door by Betty, offering only a weak lie for what they were doing. Later, Norm investigates Vault 33's Inter-Vault trade records and discovers that all of the personnel traded have been from Vault 31 to Vault 33, and all of them have ended up being elected as overseer, with Hank and Betty being the latest ones in this trend. Norm congratulates Betty at the Vault's celebration for her electoral victory. He later visits Chet in [[Steph Harper]]'s apartment to discuss his findings, but Chet dismisses them, in part because Steph herself is from Vault 31. Norm directly asks Steph about how Vault 31 is different from Vault 33; she only says that its mashed potatoes were better, causing Norm to remark that Hank said the same thing. They are later confused when Betty takes everyone to a now-cleaned Vault 32, completely devoid of any traces of the violence and death that previously occurred and announces a project to resettle the vault. Norm returns to the now-refurbished overseer's office and is joined soon after by Betty. Knowingly praising her for the successful "cleanup" of the vault, he asks Betty what happened to his mother's Pip-Boy, and is left confused when Betty claims to have buried it with Rose when she died.{{FOTV|1|5}} ====[[The Radio]]==== Back in Vault 33, Norm continues to deliver food to the imprisoned Vault 32 raiders. He arrives one day to find all of the raiders dead by poisoning, and Veronica accused of the crime. Later, when the Vault reassignment decisions are released, Norm discovers he will be staying in Vault 33. Soon, the dwellers assigned to Vault 32 prepare to leave, and Norm takes advantage of Betty's preoccupation with the departing dwellers to sneak into her office. There, he hacks into Betty's terminal and communicates with Vault 31's overseer, fooling him into opening the door to Vault 31. ====[[The Beginning]]==== Norm secretly enters Vault 31 and discovers its overseer, [[Bud Askins]], who has had his brain removed and preserved in a rudimentary [[Brain bot#Rollerbrain|rollerbrain]] chasis. He soon walks deeper into the Vault and discovers the truth: that all of its residents are cryonically frozen Vault-Tec employees from before the Great War, including his father, intended to reshape the world in the image of Vault-Tec's and Bud's own plans. Bud refuses to let Norm leave and traps him inside the cryo chamber bay, as he knows too much. Bud implores Norm to enter one of the cryo chambers so that Norm will not starve. ===Season 2=== {{Quotation|Norm is brother to Lucy, son to Hank, and one of Vault 33’s few skeptics or rebels. While he began the show as a complete coward, his curious nature has thrust him down a path of uncovering dark, dangerous secrets about his family.|[[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 2 character description]]}} ====[[The Innovator]]==== In [[Vault 31]], Norm is still locked in the cryo facility with Bud Askins, having continually refused to enter a cryopod. Bud begins to panic upon discovering that Norm had disabled inter-Vault communications and goes to check on him. Bud is unable to reach Norm, as he has sequestered himself down the stairs into the cryopod area, now littered with emptied ration cases. Bud tries to persuade Norm with his "two rational choices:" either enter Hank's cryonic chamber or starve to death. Norm asks Bud if he would ever be released from cryonic suspension; Bud says he would, but only upon achieving [[Reclamation Day (event)|Reclamation Day]], which, according to Bud, will occur when everyone on the surface who could challenge Vault-Tec's monopoly on life has died. Norm stubbornly refuses to be Bud's prisoner and insists that someone would come for him, but Bud asserts that Vault-Tec had prepared for every contingency, including when a vault dweller goes missing, promising that Betty will cover up his disappearance. To further demoralize Norm, Bud shuts off the lights, certain that he'd be more "reasonable" when he grows hungrier. Bud later checks on Norm again while he is lying on the floor. As Bud tries once again to encourage him to take Hank's pod, Norm ignores him, asking what his father was like and why he was frozen in the first place. Bud boasts that Hank was an ambitious man and that becoming one of Bud's Buds was a highly coveted position in the pre-War era. Then, noticing Norm spotted a two-headed [[centipede]], he cautions that consuming the mutated insect will cause him a slow, painful death. He instead offers to inject Norm with an unnamed poison that will give him a quick and painless death, and that when he dies, his body will dissolve and be filtered from 31 through the ventilation system into the crops for the other Vaults. Norm refuses Bud's false dichotomy of "two rational choices" and asserts there are plenty of "irrational" ones. Norm approaches Bud and kicks off the syringe limb Bud had threatened him with. Norm tells Bud that he is releasing Bud's preserved junior managers. Bud tries to protest the disruption of his plan to create a race of super managers, but is kept back with Norm's foot as Norm releases all Vault-Tec executives from their cryo-chambers. ====[[The Golden Rule]]==== Before the junior managers are thawed, Norm kills Bud Askins and places him upside down in a mop bucket. This occurs off-screen. Norm observes as the pre-War [[Vault 31 dweller]]s emerge from their stasis, greeting them. When [[Clark (TV series)|Clark]] questions why they were unfrozen all at once and where Bud Askins is, Norm claims that a change of plans was needed. When everyone decides that this means it is Reclamation Day, Norm is forced to go along with it while explaining that Bud Askins has died. This sends the assembled group into a panic, some trying to return to their pods, with Norm himself left trying to regain control. Eventually, after some thinking, Norm comes up with a speech to get everyone's attention, hawking Bud's words that he is a "super manager" created from 200 years of genetic engineering, and that the assembled Vault 31ers were unthawed to serve as his staff. He rallies the executives by saying that, while some of Bud's claims seemed outlandish before, their presence in Vault 31 is a testament to Bud's work that they must now carry on. Norm tells them that they will have proven worthy to carry on Vault-Tec's corporate strategy if they can pass a "final test" of finding a way to escape Vault 31. Invigorated by Norm's words, the 31ers begin working to salvage parts of the Vault and find a way out. Later on, the group discovers a hatch connected to the surface on the ceiling of the cryo pod bay. Norm observes as several 31ers work to form a human ladder using the machinery on the wall as footholds until one is able to unlock the hatch. He himself is obliged to take the lead and ascend up the ladder behind the hatch, connected to an old ventilation shaft. This means he is the first of the expedition to set foot into the wasteland, looking out along the nearby shoreline where he spots the remnants of the [[Santa Monica Pier]]. While the 31ers are saddened or disappointed at the state of the surface, Norm is in awe of the outside world and remarks that it is "beautiful." ====[[The Demon in the Snow]]==== The Vault 31 expedition reaches a ruined urban area of [[Los Angeles]], where they stop to raid an old [[BlamCo]] food truck and consume the uncooked [[BlamCo Mac & Cheese]] it is carrying, though Norm advises them to conserve what they find in case they cannot find more food. He then notices [[Claudia (TV series)|Claudia]] looking toward an old bridge, which she says brings back the memory of when she drove across it heading to her interview with Vault-Tec just a week before she was frozen, which Norm sympathizes with. They are then interrupted by [[Ronnie McCurtry]], who asks about their goal to start "phase two." Norm asks his name, then tries to dismiss him, saying he makes the decisions for the group. However Ronnie shrugs it off and reveals that he was Bud's personal assistant before the bombs, taking lunch orders while the executive was talking with his Vaults' investors about phase 2, "Future Enterprise Ventures," and "the plan" forVaults 32 and 33. This deflates Norm and forces him to let Ronnie take the lead of the expedition while he is left nervous about his next steps. ====[[The Wrangler]]==== Under Ronnie's direction, the expedition arrives on the grounds of the abandoned [[Vault-Tec headquarters (TV series)|Vault-Tec headquarters]]. They break through the boarded-up front doors into the lobby, where Norm discovers a fresh blood splatter and advises them to leave, though this is ignored when the group finds the remains of a former coworker. Everyone is shocked when loud bangs and skittering emits from the elevator shafts. When [[Ma June]] and [[Barv]] appear to hold them at gunpoint, the former notes with distaste that they have found "more Vault dwellers," which gets Norm's attention immediately. Norm speaks privately with Ma June, wherein she reveals her encounter with his sister at [[Filly]]. She goes on to mention several factions and recent events around Los Angeles, like the [[Enclave]], [[New California Republic|NCR]], and [[Great Khans|Khans]], but Norm clarifies that he has no idea what she is talking about. Ma apologizes for trying to talk current events to a "vaultie" and changes subjects, telling him his sister is most likely dead, but Norm refuses to believe this. Ma firmly tells him the same advice she had for his sister: "Go home." He digests that information while Ma and Barv head off again, allowing the group access to their wealth of salvage to take what they need as long as they do not mess with their [[Radroach (TV series)|radroach]] farm. Later on, Norm follows Ronnie and other managers into a comms room, which Ronnie tells him they intend to use to reach out to "the investors," giving Norm a suspicious look. Norm then sees Claudia nearby, trying to keep herself from crying. He gives her a chance to talk as she reveals she has been struggling with the fact that she has woken up 200 years after everyone she knew and loved like her parents, friends, and her cat named Puppy have died. Norm gives her reassurances before asking if she knows anything about "Future Enterprise Ventures," but Claudia denies it since she had only been in Vault-Tec for a week before the bombs. She does, however, remember the name of an executive, [[Barb Howard|Barbara Howard]], who was Bud Askins' superior and was responsible for the Vault proposals, which tips Norm off. He follows Claudia as she leads him to Barb's old office, and he tries to get into Barb's terminal. Claudia reveals that she has figured out Norm is not really Bud's successor. Norm takes this in stride, asking how she figured it out, and chuckles when she says he is not "nuts" like the other 31ers. She offers to get them both a drink, which Norm reveals he has never had one. Once Claudia leaves, he looks into Vault-Tec's database to find "Future Enterprise Ventures," but discovers there is no mention of it apart from a related search on the acronym "F.E.V." which takes him to an entry on the [[Forced Evolutionary Virus]]. Before Norm can read further, however, Ronnie, having secretly followed and heard Norm's admission to lying about being Bud's successor, pulls out the terminal's power cord and threatens Norm. Norm attempts to defend himself with a lamp but is disarmed by Ronnie and strangled with the cord. He is forced to the ground and struggles for a while before falling unconscious. ====[[The Handoff]]==== A short time after Ronnie incapacitated him, Norm wakes up on the floor of the old office, hearing the [[Vault 31 dweller]]s discussing what to do with him. Ronnie suggests they abide by a section of the Vault-Tec employee handbook that allegedly made the impersonation of management punishable by death, which the rest sycophantically go along with. [[Pete (TV series)|Pete]] then notices him waking up, and the group gathers around him as Ronnie tells [[Clark (TV series)|Clark]] to knock him out again. Norm tries to ask what the plan is for the Three Vaults but he is ignored as Clark smashes a trophy against his forehead to render him unconscious. Sometime later, Norm is reawakened by Claudia who frees his hands that were bound earlier. She tells him they have to leave but Norm responds that he has to do something first. He goes to the headquarters' communications room and uses the ham radio there to broadcast a message. First, he tries to reach out to Lucy and tell her that he is out in the wasteland and ask why she did not tell him about the Vault experiments. He then calls for his father, asking why Hank had lied to him all his life and what is going to happen to their Vault. No answer comes before Claudia alerts him to their discovery by the Vault 31 group as Norm looks on grimly. ====[[The Strip]]==== Norm is dragged through the offices by the Vault 31 dwellers as Ronnie declares they will enact a "fair trial" to decide his punishment for lying to them. Claudia tries to pull Norm away from them, but is thrown against the wall by Ronnie. This inadvertently results in her activating the controls for the elevators, opening the doors into the shafts. While Norm is on the ground, the [[executive assistant]] who was holding him goes to inspect the elevator shaft and is then attacked and killed by a [[Radroach (TV series)|radroach]]. The entire group is sent into panic as all of Ma June's radroaches fly out of the shaft and begin attacking them. Norm is left behind while the 31ers flee, managing to shield himself from a radroach by using a chair for cover. Norm tries to run after the fleeing 31ers, briefly stopping to save the last 31er, who had fallen to the ground and was being attacked. However, Ronnie refuses to let him into the break room all of the 31ers are taking cover in; though both Norm and Claudia try to resist, Norm is ultimately shoved to the ground by Ronnie, making him unable to get in before the radroach swarm comes. However, Ronnie's delay in closing the door allows the radroaches to overpower him, sweeping into the break room and slaughtering the 31ers. Ironically, Norm manages to survive by ducking under a nearby table, where he is ignored by the radroaches, all of whom swarmed into the break room, with its door closing amidst the chaos. Norm is forced to listen to the 31ers' dying screams. Later, after the room had gone quiet, Norm crawls out and goes in to investigate, seeing the carnage with nearly every Vault 31 dweller and at least some of the radroaches dead. He manages to find Claudia still alive, but wounded. After recovering some supplies and improvising a sled, Norm harnesses himself to it to take Claudia with him as they leave the headquarters, promising to get her "home." ==Personality== [[File:Betty and Norm.png|thumb|250px|Norm speaking to Betty]] Norm is a clever young man who begins the series as a somewhat timid and apathetic individual but gradually becomes more confident as the series progresses. He seems to enjoy teasing others, such as when he tells Lucy her future husband might be a cannibal. Betty also figures out that Norm likes to upset people, although it also seems Norm simply prefers speaking his mind even if it makes him seem rude to others. Nevertheless, he maintains a sense of innocence that is common among Vault dwellers who have never been to the surface. Norm is also a perceptive individual, being one of the first to figure out that something is wrong with the "dwellers" from Vault 32 before they were revealed as raiders. Over time, Norm is shown to exhibit a great amount of bravery, having the courage to let his sister out of the Vault and exploring the decrepit Vaults 31 and 32. This stems from his regret over hiding in a duct while raiders attacked Vault 33, which spurs him to become more active. He is also shown to be somewhat vindictive, particularly towards the raiders, wishing them dead. That said, when it is discovered later that the raiders had been mysteriously killed from consuming rat poison in their food, Norm did not show joy. In the quiet life in the Vault, he does not seem to enjoy his family's book club; instead, he prefers to play Pip-Boy games. After being imprisoned in Vault 31 by [[Bud Askins]] to keep the secret of the Vault experiments, Norm shows a more ruthless side such as taking steps to sabotage Bud's controls and eventually upending his entire plan by thawing out the Vault 31 dwellers, ultimately killing Bud himself by destroying his robotic chassis. He demonstrates his cunning by crafting a story to the unfrozen Bud's Buds executives that he is Bud's successor and their leader in trying to escape Vault 31 and start reclaiming the surface. Despite the fact that he lies to them, Norm is still capable of empathy for the pre-War managers such as hearing Claudia reminisce about her pre-War life and later comforting her after she opens up about her sadness at losing everyone she knew and loved while she was frozen. He continues to show his empathy when he tries to save one of them who had fallen down during the radroach attack, later showing terror and sadness after being forced to listen to their dying screams as the swarm slaughters them. He waits until it stops to go in and recover a wounded Claudia, bringing her with him to find a safe place. ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|And as for his looks? Big butt? No butt? But of course, it's just superficial concerns, it's what's on the inside that counts. And in that respect, he could be a cannibal, or just like crammed full of tumors.|sound=Norm for his looks.ogg|Norm talking to Lucy about her prospective husband}} * {{Inline quote|No, but that sounds accurate.|sound=Norm sounds accurate.ogg|Norm when asked if he knows his performance reviews have all been "lacks enthusiasm" in "[[The Head]]"}} * {{Inline quote|I don't know, I don't think it's our job to help these people. They're murderers.|sound=Norm theyre murderers.ogg|Norm regarding the Vault 32 raiders in "The Head"}} ==Appearances== Norm MacLean appears {{in|FOTV}}. He was also added to ''[[Fallout Shelter]]'' in update 1.17.0. {{FOTV appearances |1=101 |3=103 |4=104 |5=105 |7=107 |8=108 |9=201 |10=202 |12=204 |13=205 |15=207 |16=208 }} ==Behind the scenes== * Norm appears in six out of eight episodes in the first season and is the most frequently recurring character outside of Lucy, who appears in all eight episodes, and [[Maximus]] and [[the Ghoul]], who appear in seven each. ** Although Norm can be considered a major character of the show, he was not explicitly called a protagonist in any Amazon descriptions for season 1, nor was he featured in promotional marketing that focused on Lucy, Maximus, and the Ghoul. However, Moisés Arias is also credited as part of the main cast in episodes in which he appears, and Norm does play a leading role outside of the three main protagonists and thus could be considered a deuteragonist of the series. * Norm's actor, [[Moisés Arias]], is 4 feet and 11 inches (1.50m) tall. Compared to the rest of his family, Hank's actor, [[Kyle MacLachlan]], is 6 feet (1.83m) tall, and Lucy and Chet are of average height, although it is unclear how tall Rose's actress, [[Elle Vertes]], is. * {{Note|(Age)}} Moisés Arias is older than Lucy's actress, [[Ella Purnell]]. However, Norm is referred to as both older and younger than Lucy in various places: ** In the [[The End script|script]] for "[[The End (episode)|The End]]," Norm is referenced as being 22,{{inline quote|REVEAL: It’s not just the two of them at the dining table. Lucy’s older brother NORM (22, brilliant but unmotivated) is also there, playing a game on his Pip-Boy as his sister and father talk excitedly about the book.|[[The End script|"The End" script]], p. 10}} while Lucy is said to be 20.{{inline quote|VERY CLOSE ON: LUCY MACLEAN (20), reading a statement she has prepared.|[[The End script|"The End" script]], p. 7}} However, Norm's official [[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|character description for ''Fallout'' season 1 on Amazon Prime]] calls him Lucy's younger brother, while the descriptions for ''Fallout'' season 2 only refers to him as her brother.
